quote: It takes longer for subjects to name this color
content: This is the Stroop effect (Stroop, 1935), and it is among the most robust and endlessly replicated findings in all of psychology—the interference is large, reliable across decades, languages, and laboratories, and well characterized theoretically (MacLeod's review, 1991). An entirely safe example to lean on.

quote: Cognitive causes are ontologically distinct from evolutionary causes.
content: Correct and important: this is Mayr's proximate/ultimate distinction (1961) and the heart of Tinbergen's four questions (1963). A trait's evolutionary history (why selection built it) and its mechanism (how it runs now) are different levels of explanation, and conflating them—reading inclusive-fitness goals into the felt content of an emotion—is exactly the confusion biologists are trained to avoid. The framework being invoked is mainstream and well founded.

quote: which would have been fertility cues in the ancestral environment
content: The proximate/ultimate logic is sound, but the specific adaptationist content slipped into the vignette is precisely the contested part of evolutionary psychology. Buss's cross-cultural survey (1989) did find men weighting youth and looks and women weighting resources, but the adaptationist reading is disputed: the sex difference shrinks markedly in more gender-equal societies (Zentner & Mitura, 2012), which fits a sociostructural account at least as well. Presenting "clear complexion = fertility cue" and "confident smile = resource-provisioning cue" as plain fact illustrates the field's habit of confident reverse-engineering from a trait to its supposed ancestral function.
